subject: Add net_id/prev_net_id to the watch-tick shadow observation so it can validate the reload path
description:
Found 2026-08-17 while reviewing the Rust-port shadow (194/201 identical, 08-08..08-17).
Filed originally as native-harness task #12; migrated to taskq 2026-08-30.

Divergence bundle ~/.config/rowt/log/parity/20260814-131118:
  plan (rust):    journal unknown / next settle / corp-sync / write-net-id 172.20.10.3/172.20.10.1 / next stop
  actual (shell): ...same... + log network change (iface 'en0' -> 'en0', [172.20.10.3/172.20.10.1], service 'Wi-Fi') — reloading
                              + audit BEGIN watchdog reload + reload

The observation record handed to the Rust planner is:
  active_service, boot_matches, captive, host_running, iface, intent, mode,
  proxy_any_on, proxy_intent, proxy_pointing_ok

It carries NO network identity. The reload was triggered by the ADDRESS pair changing
(iface was en0 both before and after — the machine moved to a hotspot, 172.20.10.x),
and that field is simply absent, so the Rust planner structurally cannot reproduce
the decision.

Why it matters more than one bundle: auto-reload on network change is the single most
important thing the watchdog does, and the shadow cannot exercise it at all. Every
"identical" verdict on that path is uninformative — the evidence has a hole in exactly
the place the shadow exists to de-risk, and the Phase 3 tick cutover is gated on that
evidence.

Fix: add net_id + prev_net_id (and the active-service name if the shell's compare uses
it) to the observation the shadow captures, then confirm a network change produces a
matching plan. The comparison is bash-vs-Rust, so BOTH sides must move together.

Definition of done: a shadow bundle covering a real network change (address pair moves,
iface unchanged) where the Rust plan includes the reload the shell took, and the
watch-tick gate in tests/parity/ covers it.

Not urgent / no live impact: the Rust tick is shadow-only; bash still runs the real tick.

NOT a bug, don't chase it: bundle 20260813-185840 is a race — obs said host_running=True,
the shell then found the router down and recovered it. Two samples, two different worlds.
The five bundles dated 2026-08-10 predate the comparator fix and are already explained.
activeForm: Adding net-id to the watch-tick shadow observation
